modules.title: Meaning, Terms and Principles
modules.html:
Meaning

Insurance is a contract in which the insurer, for a consideration called the premium, undertakes to indemnify the insured against loss arising from a specified risk. It works by pooling risks: the contributions of many meet the misfortunes of a few.

Basic Terms

TermMeaning
InsurerThe company that accepts the risk
Insured/assuredThe person whose risk is covered
PremiumPeriodic payment for cover
PolicyWritten contract of insurance
Proposal formApplication giving material facts
Cover noteTemporary evidence of insurance
Surrender valueAmount paid if a life policy is discontinued early
ActuaryExpert who calculates risk and premium

Principles of Insurance

  1. Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) – both parties must disclose all material facts.
  2. Insurable interest – the insured must stand to lose financially if the event occurs.
  3. Indemnity – the insured is restored to his former position, no more; does not apply to life and personal accident.
  4. Subrogation – after full settlement the insurer takes over the remains/rights of the insured.
  5. Contribution – where several insurers cover the same risk, each pays a proportionate share.
  6. Proximate cause – the nearest, most effective cause of loss must be an insured peril.

Insurable vs Non-insurable Risks

Insurable: fire, theft, motor accident, death, marine perils – they are measurable and occur to many. Non-insurable: loss from bad management, changes in fashion, fall in demand, gambling losses, war (usually), and deliberate acts of the insured.

examples.q: A man insures his neighbour's house against fire. Is the contract valid?
examples.a: No. He has no insurable interest – he suffers no direct financial loss if the house burns. The contract is void and amounts to a wager; premiums may simply be refunded.

examples.q: A trader insures goods worth ₦4,000,000 with Insurer A for ₦3,000,000 and Insurer B for ₦1,000,000. A total loss occurs. How much does each pay?
examples.a: By the principle of contribution, A pays \( \dfrac{3}{4}\times4{,}000{,}000 = ₦3{,}000{,}000 \) and B pays \( \dfrac{1}{4}\times4{,}000{,}000 = ₦1{,}000{,}000 \). Together they indemnify, but the insured cannot recover more than his actual loss.

modules.title: Classes of Insurance
modules.html:
1. Life Assurance

  • Whole life – premiums until death; sum paid to beneficiaries.
  • Endowment – payable at a fixed date or earlier death; combines saving and protection.
  • Term assurance – pays only if death occurs within the stated term.
  • Annuity – regular income paid for life in exchange for a lump sum.

It is called assurance because the event (death) is certain; only its timing is uncertain. Indemnity does not apply.

2. Marine Insurance

Covers hull, cargo, freight and shipowner's liability. Types of loss:

  • Total loss – actual or constructive.
  • Particular average – partial loss borne by the owner of the damaged goods alone.
  • General average – deliberate sacrifice (e.g. jettison) for the common safety; shared by all interests.
  • Salvage charges – cost of saving the ship or cargo.

3. Fire, Motor and Accident Insurance

ClassCover
FireDamage by fire, lightning, explosion; extensions for riot and flood
Motor – third partyCompulsory; injury/damage to third parties only
Motor – third party fire & theftThird party plus fire/theft of own vehicle
Motor – comprehensiveAll the above plus own damage
Employers' liability / workmen's compensationInjury to employees at work
Fidelity guaranteeDishonesty of employees
Burglary, consequential loss (business interruption), professional indemnityOther accident classes

Reinsurance, Co-insurance and Double Insurance

  • Reinsurance – an insurer passes part of a very large risk to another insurer (e.g. Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation).
  • Co-insurance – two or more insurers share one risk from the outset, each on its own share.
  • Double insurance – the same risk insured with more than one insurer by the insured; contribution applies.

examples.q: During a storm, cargo worth ₦8,000,000 is jettisoned to save a ship and its remaining cargo worth ₦72,000,000. Explain the settlement.
examples.a: This is a general average loss because the sacrifice was deliberate and for the common safety. The ₦8,000,000 is shared rateably by all interests saved. If the ship and cargo saved total ₦72,000,000, each party contributes \( \dfrac{8{,}000{,}000}{72{,}000{,}000} \approx 11.1\% \) of its saved value.

examples.q: Goods worth ₦10,000,000 are insured for only ₦6,000,000 (average clause applies). A fire destroys ₦4,500,000 worth. How much is paid?
examples.a: Under-insurance triggers the average clause: \( \text{Claim} = \dfrac{\text{Sum Insured}}{\text{Value of Property}} \times \text{Loss} = \dfrac{6{,}000{,}000}{10{,}000{,}000}\times4{,}500{,}000 = ₦2{,}700{,}000 \). The insured bears the remaining ₦1,800,000 as his own insurer.

modules.title: Premiums, Claims and the Role of Insurance in Commerce
modules.html:
Computing Premium

$$\text{Premium} = \text{Sum Insured} \times \text{Rate}$$

Rates reflect the degree of risk, the record of the insured, the value of the property and any no-claim discount.

Average Clause

$$\text{Claim Payable} = \dfrac{\text{Sum Insured}}{\text{Value of Property}} \times \text{Actual Loss}$$

Contribution

$$\text{Share of Insurer A} = \dfrac{\text{Policy A}}{\text{Total Policies}} \times \text{Loss}$$

Importance of Insurance to Business

  1. Transfers risk, giving confidence to invest and expand.
  2. Makes credit possible – lenders insist on cover.
  3. Provides a pool of investible funds for the economy.
  4. Encourages international trade through marine and credit insurance.
  5. Provides social security and employment.

Regulation in Nigeria

Insurance business is supervised by NAICOM (National Insurance Commission). Compulsory covers in Nigeria include motor third-party, group life for employers, builders' liability and occupiers' liability.

examples.q: A factory worth ₦80,000,000 is insured at a rate of 1.5% with a 20% no-claim discount. Calculate the annual premium.
Explain how insurance supports a bank's willingness to grant a business loan.
examples.a: The bank's security – stock, buildings or the borrower's life – may be destroyed. With a fire or life policy assigned to the bank, loss is compensated and the loan can still be repaid. Insurance therefore converts an uncertain risk into a fixed, small cost, and makes lending safer and cheaper.

quiz.q: Insurance operates on the principle of
quiz.solution: Contributions of many insured persons meet the losses of the unfortunate few.

quiz.q: Which principle requires full disclosure of material facts?
quiz.solution: Uberrimae fidei obliges both parties to disclose all material facts.
Human life cannot be valued in money, so life assurance is not a contract of indemnity.

quiz.q: The right of the insurer to take over damaged property after full payment is
quiz.solution: Subrogation prevents the insured from profiting twice from one loss.

quiz.q: If property worth ₦10m is insured for ₦5m and a loss of ₦2m occurs, the average clause gives a claim of
Deliberate sacrifice of cargo for the safety of a ship is
quiz.solution: General average loss is shared by all interests benefiting from the sacrifice.

quiz.q: A risk that CANNOT be insured is
quiz.solution: Losses arising from poor management or changes in fashion are not measurable or fortuitous.

quiz.q: Motor insurance that is compulsory in Nigeria is
quiz.solution: Third-party motor cover is required by law.

quiz.q: A temporary document issued before the policy is prepared is a
quiz.solution: The cover note gives interim evidence of insurance.

quiz.q: Where an insurer passes part of a large risk to another insurer, this is
quiz.solution: Reinsurance spreads a risk that is too large for one company.

quiz.q: Premium on a ₦40,000,000 property at 2% is
The person who calculates insurance risks and premiums is a(n)
quiz.solution: An actuary uses statistics and probability to fix premiums.

quiz.q: Insurable interest in a fire policy must exist
options: Only at the time of loss
At the time of taking the policy and at loss
quiz.solution: For property insurance, insurable interest must exist at inception and at the time of loss.

quiz.q: The amount paid when a life policy is discontinued early is the
quiz.solution: Surrender value is the cash payable on early termination.

quiz.q: Insurance in Nigeria is regulated by
quiz.solution: The National Insurance Commission supervises insurers and brokers.

quiz.q: Two insurers each cover the same ₦8m risk equally; a loss of ₦3m occurs. Each pays
quiz.solution: By contribution each bears half of the ₦3m loss = ₦1.5m; the insured is indemnified once.
